parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Enumerate $(B,G,A)=(2,1,2),(2,2,1),(2,3,0),(3,1,1),(3,2,0)$ using $\binom3B\binom4G\binom5A$. [M1]
Guidance: Use products $\binom3x\binom4y\binom5z$ for category counts summing to 5; permutation notation may gain this method mark.
For example, $\binom32\binom41\binom52=120$ and $\binom32\binom42\binom51=90$. [B1]
Guidance: At least two appropriate cases are correctly identified, including unsimplified forms.
$120+90+12+20+6$. [M1]
Guidance: Sum four or five correct identified cases only, with no repeats or extra cases.
$120+90+12+20+6=248$. [A1]
Guidance: Final total 248 depends only on the two method marks.
Total: 4

parts.label: (c)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
After fixing the endpoint adults, arrange the three-boy block and the seven remaining individuals as eight units in $8!$ ways. [M1]
Guidance: Arrange the boy block and seven remaining non-end people as eight units; accept an equivalent $8!$ factor.
Arrange the three distinct boys within their block in $3!$ ways. [M1]
Guidance: Account for all $3!$ internal orders of the three distinct boys.
Choose and order two of the five adults at the ends in ${}^{5}P_2$ ways, giving $8!\times3!\times{}^{5}P_2$. [M1]
Guidance: Select and order two of the five adults at the ends using ${}^{5}P_2$ or $2\binom52$; extra terms limit method credit.
$8!\times3!\times{}^{5}P_2=4\,838\,400$. [A1]
Guidance: Exact value required.
Total: 4
